recommendation: Keep the no-change audit. If a future build still resolves the synchronicity value set link to the Extension Pack instead of the core page, fix build/kindling packaging behavior or Extension Pack publication metadata rather than changing the current core source definitions.
issue_request: FHIR-52426 was Applied/Persuasive for R6 by FHIR-I. It observed that OperationDefinition.synchronicity is a code element with a required binding to ValueSet/synchronicity-control and requested moving the CodeSystem and ValueSet from the Extension Pack into FHIR core.
initial_application: No FHIR repository source commit mentioning FHIR-52426 was found, and the Jira comment says the applied change was in kindling. Current source already contains source/operationdefinition/codesystem-synchronicity-control.xml and source/operationdefinition/valueset-synchronicity-control.xml from the earlier FHIR-41202 application commit.
additional_context: The related committers Zulip thread records the policy reason: a core code element with a required binding should not depend on extension-pack terminology. FHIR-I minutes for 2025-09-22 record that the code system and value set need to move to core and the URL stays the same, so the change is not breaking. The Extension Pack still carries R6-sourced copies for extension use, while the core checkout has the authoritative R6 source files.
reconciliation: No source change was needed. The current FHIR core source already includes the synchronicity CodeSystem and ValueSet under the active OperationDefinition resource and OperationDefinition.synchronicity binds to that canonical value set.
